verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is a changelog note that PlanetScale Postgres exposes PgBouncer graphs in its dashboard, which implies a PlanetScale-run PgBouncer pooler so users don't operate their own. Nothing documents how it is configured or how many concurrent connections it handles. Missing for 10: first-party docs describing the built-in pooler and its configuration, evidence it handles thousands of concurrent connections, connection limits or scaling behavior, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, a built-in connection pooler handles thousands of concurrent connections without me operating my own pgbouncer or proxy

citations.quote: Postgres instance, storage, and PgBouncer graphs now live on their own tabs with shareable URLs.
